🍌 Banana Calorie Calculator

Calculate how many calories are in a banana by weight, size or number of bananas. See estimated carbohydrates, sugars, fibre, protein and potassium for your portion.

Choose the approximate edible weight without the peel. Ripeness affects texture and sugar composition, but its effect on total calories is not reliably represented by a fixed percentage.

Enter an amount or select a banana size

Banana calories by size

The calories in a banana depend mainly on its edible weight. These estimates use approximately 89 calories per 100g of raw banana flesh.

Serving Edible weight Calories
Small banana ~81g 72 kcal
Medium banana ~105g 93 kcal
Large banana ~126g 112 kcal
Extra-large banana ~152g 135 kcal
Half a large banana ~63g 56 kcal
Two medium bananas ~210g 187 kcal

These are approximate values. Banana length and weight vary, so weighing the peeled fruit gives a more precise estimate.

Banana nutrition per 100g

Bananas provide carbohydrates for energy, along with fibre, potassium and small amounts of protein and fat. The table below compares typical values per 100g with a large banana weighing approximately 126g without its peel.

Nutrient Per 100g Large banana (126g)
Calories 89 kcal 112 kcal
Carbohydrates 22.8g 28.7g
— Sugars 12.2g 15.4g
— Fibre 2.6g 3.3g
Protein 1.1g 1.4g
Fat 0.3g 0.4g
Potassium 358mg 451mg
Magnesium 27mg 34mg
Vitamin B6 0.37mg 0.47mg
Vitamin C 8.7mg 11mg

Nutritional values are averages for raw banana flesh and may vary with variety, growing conditions and ripeness.

How many calories are in half a banana?

Half a banana contains roughly half the calories of a whole banana of the same size. Half a medium banana (about 52g of edible flesh) provides around 47 calories, while half a large banana (about 63g) provides approximately 56 calories.

If you are tracking your food intake, weigh the portion after peeling it. This avoids including the weight of the peel, which is not normally eaten.

Are bananas good for sport and exercise?

Bananas are a convenient snack before or after exercise. They provide carbohydrates that the body can use for energy, as well as potassium and vitamin B6. A large banana contains around 112 calories and 29g of carbohydrates, making it a practical option before a workout or as part of a recovery meal.

As a banana ripens, some of its starch is converted into sugars, changing its sweetness and texture. Green bananas generally contain more resistant starch, while ripe bananas tend to taste sweeter. The exact effect on digestion and blood glucose varies from person to person and with the rest of the meal.

How to calculate banana calories

The calculator uses an average reference value of 89 calories per 100g of edible banana. Enter the weight of the peeled banana, choose a size, or select the number of bananas to estimate the calories in your portion.

Formula

Calories = edible weight in grams × 89 ÷ 100

For example, a banana with 120g of edible flesh contains approximately 107 calories. The result is an estimate, not a laboratory measurement of the specific fruit you eat.

Do bananas make you gain weight?

Eating bananas does not automatically cause weight gain. A banana provides carbohydrates, fibre and several micronutrients, with around 89 calories per 100g of edible flesh. Weight change depends on overall energy intake and expenditure over time, rather than on one particular food.

Frequently asked questions

How many calories are in a banana?

A small banana (about 81g of edible flesh) contains approximately 72 calories. A medium banana (105g) has around 93 calories, and a large banana (126g) has about 112 calories.

How many calories are in half a banana?

Half a medium banana contains around 47 calories, while half a large banana contains about 56 calories. The exact amount depends on the weight of the edible portion.

Does a green banana have fewer calories than a ripe banana?

The total calorie content is broadly similar for bananas of the same weight. Ripening changes the balance between starch and sugars, so a ripe banana usually tastes sweeter, while a greener banana contains more resistant starch.

How much potassium is in a banana?

A large banana weighing around 126g provides approximately 451mg of potassium. The exact amount varies with the size and composition of the fruit.

Can I eat bananas while trying to lose weight?

Yes. Bananas can fit into a weight-loss diet. They provide fibre and can be a convenient, satisfying snack. Portion size and your overall eating pattern matter more than avoiding one specific fruit.

Should I weigh a banana with or without the peel?

Weigh the banana after peeling it. The calculator uses edible flesh only, so including the peel would overestimate the portion you eat.
